parameters.query:
-- Claim leads that are ready for a first message, and open their run in the
-- same statement so the agent_runs row is the claim.
--
-- The recipient must have a usable address and must not be suppressed. Both
-- are checked again downstream - suppression by the trigger on outreach - but
-- checking here is what stops a draft being written for somebody unreachable
-- and costing a model call to find out.
WITH claimed AS (
    SELECT l.id
    FROM leads l
    JOIN people p    ON p.id = l.person_id
    JOIN companies c ON c.id = l.company_id
    WHERE l.status = 'new'
      AND l.score >= ($1::jsonb ->> 'min_score')::int
      AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM outreach o WHERE o.lead_id = l.id AND o.sequence_step = 1
      )
      -- A draft needs somewhere to go. is_suppressed(NULL) is false and the
      -- trigger on outreach has nothing to compare against, so a lead whose
      -- recipient has no address reaches pending_approval addressed to nobody:
      -- measured on Adyen, where WF-03 derived an address for the chief
      -- executive, WF-04 created the lead on it, and the address was withdrawn
      -- an hour later because his surname is "van der Does".
      --
      -- WF-04 checks this when it creates the lead. It has to be checked again
      -- here because an address can be withdrawn or bounce between the two, and
      -- the same three statuses are what people_contactable_idx already calls
      -- contactable.
      AND p.email IS NOT NULL
      AND p.email_status IN ('valid', 'catch_all', 'guessed')
      AND NOT is_suppressed(p.email)
      AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1 FROM agent_runs r
          WHERE r.agent_name = 'outreach'
            AND r.status     = 'running'
            AND (r.input ->> 'lead_id')::uuid = l.id
            AND r.started_at > now() - interval '15 minutes'
      )
    ORDER BY l.score DESC, l.created_at
    LIMIT ($1::jsonb ->> 'batch_size')::int
    FOR UPDATE OF l SKIP LOCKED
),
opened AS (
    INSERT INTO agent_runs (agent_name, company_id, input, status, model, started_at)
    SELECT 'outreach', l.company_id,
           ($1::jsonb -> 'input') || jsonb_build_object('lead_id', l.id),
           'running', $1::jsonb ->> 'model', now()
    FROM claimed JOIN leads l ON l.id = claimed.id
    RETURNING id AS agent_run_id, (input ->> 'lead_id')::uuid AS lead_id
)
SELECT o.agent_run_id,
       l.id AS lead_id,
       l.score,
       l.reason AS lead_reason,
       l.recommended_offer,
       c.id AS company_id,
       c.name AS company_name,
       c.domain::text AS domain,
       c.industry,
       c.employee_count,
       c.description,
       p.full_name  AS person_name,
       split_part(p.full_name, ' ', 1) AS person_first_name,
       p.title      AS person_title,
       p.email::text AS person_email,
       COALESCE((
           SELECT r.output -> 'analysis'
           FROM agent_runs r
           WHERE r.company_id = c.id AND r.agent_name = 'research' AND r.status = 'success'
           ORDER BY r.finished_at DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1
       ), '{}'::jsonb) AS research_analysis,
       COALESCE((
           SELECT json_agg(json_build_object(
                      'signal_type', s.signal_type, 'signal', s.signal,
                      'source_url', s.source_url, 'confidence', s.confidence)
                  ORDER BY s.created_at)
           FROM signals s WHERE s.company_id = c.id
       ), '[]'::json) AS signals,
       -- Every URL the research actually found, from both places it lands.
       -- hook_source must be one of these or the human approving the draft
       -- cannot check the one claim the message rests on.
       COALESCE((
           SELECT json_agg(DISTINCT src)
           FROM (
               SELECT jsonb_array_elements_text(
                          COALESCE(r.output #> '{analysis,sources}', '[]'::jsonb)) AS src
               FROM agent_runs r
               WHERE r.company_id = c.id AND r.agent_name = 'research' AND r.status = 'success'
               UNION
               SELECT s.source_url FROM signals s
               WHERE s.company_id = c.id AND s.source_url IS NOT NULL
           ) u
           WHERE src IS NOT NULL AND src <> ''
       ), '[]'::json) AS known_sources
FROM opened o
JOIN leads l     ON l.id = o.lead_id
JOIN people p    ON p.id = l.person_id
JOIN companies c ON c.id = l.company_id;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ batch_size: 5, min_score: Number($env.OUTREACH_MIN_SCORE) || 60, model: $env.OLLAMA_OUTREACH_MODEL || $env.OLLAMA_RESEARCH_MODEL || 'qwen9-64k:latest', input: { execution_id: String($execution.id), workflow_id: $workflow.id, stage: 'outreach' } } ) }}

parameters.query:
-- The draft passed every check. It goes to pending_approval, which is where it
-- stops: Phase 1-7, nothing leaves that status without a human.
WITH payload AS (SELECT $1::jsonb AS p),
ins AS (
    INSERT INTO outreach (lead_id, channel, sequence_step, subject, body, status)
    SELECT (payload.p ->> 'lead_id')::uuid, 'email', 1,
           payload.p #>> '{draft,subject}',
           payload.p #>> '{draft,body}',
           'pending_approval'
    FROM payload
    ON CONFLICT (lead_id, sequence_step) DO UPDATE
        SET subject = EXCLUDED.subject,
            body    = EXCLUDED.body,
            status  = 'pending_approval',
            rejection_reason = NULL
    RETURNING id, status
),
lead AS (
    UPDATE leads
    SET status = 'pending_approval'
    FROM payload
    WHERE leads.id = (payload.p ->> 'lead_id')::uuid
      AND leads.status = 'new'
    RETURNING id
)
SELECT (SELECT id FROM ins)              AS outreach_id,
       (SELECT status FROM ins)          AS outreach_status,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM lead)::int  AS leads_moved,
       $1::jsonb ->> 'agent_run_id'      AS agent_run_id;

parameters.query:
-- Two non-sending outcomes in one statement, told apart by 'outcome'.
--
-- 'blocked': a check failed. The draft is stored at 'draft' with the reason so a
-- human can read what the model actually wrote. It is never edited to comply -
-- docs/workflows.md: it is never auto-corrected.
--
-- 'not_sending': the agent judged there was nothing worth writing. No draft
-- exists to store. The lead moves to 'nurture' so it leaves the queue instead of
-- being re-generated every hour.
WITH payload AS (SELECT $1::jsonb AS p),
ins AS (
    INSERT INTO outreach (lead_id, channel, sequence_step, subject, body, status, rejection_reason)
    SELECT (payload.p ->> 'lead_id')::uuid, 'email', 1,
           payload.p #>> '{draft,subject}',
           payload.p #>> '{draft,body}',
           'draft',
           payload.p ->> 'block_reason'
    FROM payload
    WHERE payload.p ->> 'outcome' = 'blocked'
    ON CONFLICT (lead_id, sequence_step) DO UPDATE
        SET subject          = EXCLUDED.subject,
            body             = EXCLUDED.body,
            status           = 'draft',
            rejection_reason = EXCLUDED.rejection_reason
    RETURNING id
),
nurtured AS (
    UPDATE leads
    SET status = 'nurture'
    FROM payload
    WHERE leads.id = (payload.p ->> 'lead_id')::uuid
      AND payload.p ->> 'outcome' = 'not_sending'
      AND leads.status = 'new'
    RETURNING id
)
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM ins)::int      AS drafts_blocked,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM nurtured)::int AS leads_nurtured,
       $1::jsonb ->> 'outcome'              AS outcome,
       $1::jsonb ->> 'agent_run_id'         AS agent_run_id;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ lead_id: $json.lead_id, agent_run_id: $json.agent_run_id, outcome: $json.outcome, draft: $json.draft, block_reason: $json.block_reason } ) }}

parameters.query:
UPDATE agent_runs
SET status        = 'success',
    output        = $1::jsonb -> 'output',
    error         = NULL,
    prompt_tokens = ($1::jsonb #>> '{usage,prompt_tokens}')::int,
    output_tokens = ($1::jsonb #>> '{usage,completion_tokens}')::int,
    finished_at   = now()
WHERE id = ($1::jsonb ->> 'agent_run_id')::uuid
RETURNING id, company_id, status, duration_ms;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ agent_run_id: $('Validate And Check').item.json.agent_run_id, usage: $('Validate And Check').item.json.usage, output: { outcome: $('Validate And Check').item.json.outcome, blocks: $('Validate And Check').item.json.blocks, notes: $('Validate And Check').item.json.notes, draft: $('Validate And Check').item.json.draft, model_output: $('Validate And Check').item.json.model_output } } ) }}

parameters.query:
-- The model failed or returned something unusable. No draft was written and the
-- lead stays at 'new', so the next hourly pass tries again.
UPDATE agent_runs
SET status      = 'error',
    error       = COALESCE(NULLIF($1::jsonb ->> 'error', ''), 'Outreach failed with no message'),
    output      = $1::jsonb -> 'output',
    finished_at = now()
WHERE id = ($1::jsonb ->> 'agent_run_id')::uuid
RETURNING id, company_id, status, error;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ agent_run_id: $json.agent_run_id, error: $json.error_message, output: { errors: $json.errors, raw_response: $json.raw_response } } ) }}

parameters.query:
-- Queue the approval message described in docs/telegram.md.
--
-- The layout is not arbitrary and the comments in that document explain each
-- rule: the hook and its source come BEFORE the body, because the one thing
-- worth checking is whether the claim is true and that takes five seconds if
-- the link is at the top; and the whole body is shown, because an approval on
-- a summary is not an approval.
--
-- Everything except the hook is read from v_approval_queue, so the message
-- describes the row that was actually written, not what the workflow believes
-- it wrote. The hook comes in as a parameter because it lives in the agent's
-- output rather than in the outreach row.
--
-- Zero rows out means the draft was not found at pending_approval and nothing
-- is queued. That is a refused write, not a silent success.
WITH q AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM v_approval_queue
    WHERE outreach_id = ($1::jsonb ->> 'outreach_id')::uuid
),
composed AS (
    SELECT q.outreach_id,
           q.lead_id,
           q.company_id,
           'Draft ready: ' || q.company_name || ' — ' || q.full_name AS title,
           '[' || q.score_band || ' ' || COALESCE(q.score::text, '?') || ']  '
               || q.company_name || '  (' || q.domain || ')'
           || E'\n' || q.full_name || COALESCE(', ' || q.title, '')
           || E'\n' || 'Offer: ' || COALESCE(q.recommended_offer, 'none')
           || E'\n\n' || 'Hook: '   || COALESCE(NULLIF($1::jsonb ->> 'hook_fact',   ''), '(none recorded)')
           || E'\n'   || 'Source: ' || COALESCE(NULLIF($1::jsonb ->> 'hook_source', ''), '(none recorded)')
           || E'\n\n' || 'Subject: ' || COALESCE(q.subject, '(none)')
           || E'\n\n' || q.body
           -- docs/telegram.md specifies /approve and /reject here. They are not
           -- built yet, and printing a command that does nothing would be worse
           -- than printing none, so the id is given and the gap is stated.
           || E'\n\n' || 'id ' || left(q.outreach_id::text, 4)
               || '  ·  approve and reject still happen in the database; the Telegram commands are not built yet'
               AS body
    FROM q
)
SELECT n.notification_id, n.status, n.occurrences, n.deduplicated,
       composed.outreach_id, composed.lead_id
FROM composed
CROSS JOIN LATERAL queue_notification(
    'draft_ready',
    'draft_ready:' || composed.outreach_id,
    composed.title,
    composed.body,
    -- Batched: a draft is not an emergency, and docs/telegram.md puts it in the
    -- batched row of its notification table.
    'batched',
    jsonb_build_object('outreach_id', composed.outreach_id, 'lead_id', composed.lead_id),
    composed.company_id,
    composed.lead_id,
    interval '7 days'
) n;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ outreach_id: $json.outreach_id, hook_fact: $('Validate And Check').item.json.draft.hook_fact, hook_source: $('Validate And Check').item.json.draft.hook_source } ) }}
